articles.title: NFL referee faces 112-mile dash on double-duty Sunday after FAA ground stop
articles.summary: Don Willard faces 112-mile trip between NFL games. NBA scrambles to replace referees stranded by delays. College football games postponed as teams struggle. An NFL official will work two games on the same day Sunday after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide for…
body: Don Willard will officiate the Miami Dolphins’ game against the Indianapolis Colts at 1pm ET before traveling 112 miles east to work the Pittsburgh Steelers’ Sunday Night Football matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The NFL benefited from its Sunday schedule, with teams typically traveling the day before their games. But Friday’s flight stoppage forced adjustments across the league’s officiating crews and elsewhere in American sports.
The NBA also made changes to its officiating assignments as travel disruptions continued into Saturday.

Brian Forte was added to the officiating crew for the Chicago-Minnesota game, replacing Jason Goldenberg. Jenna Schroeder, meanwhile, replaced Forte for the Dallas-Cleveland game. The Brooklyn-Memphis game brought Michael Smith into the three-person crew late in the afternoon after another referee could not get there in time.

articles.title: Fiji 'did Ireland a favour' before South Africa game
articles.summary: Former South Africa head coach Jake White says his Fiji side "did Ireland a favour" in Saturday's Nations Championship match before they face the Springboks in Dublin next week.
body: Fiji lost 43-15 to Ireland at Aviva Stadium having frustrated Andy Farrell's side during a closely contested first half.

While Ireland scored 26 unanswered points in the second half, White - who led South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007 - suggested Farrell's team cannot afford similarly sluggish spells against the back-to-back world champions, who won 24-13 in Dublin last year.
"We were playing a little bit like South Africa to be honest, I think that sums it up," said the 62-year-old.
"We were letting Ireland have the ball and we were happy to defend against them and we were happy for them to try to outwork us."

articles.title: Andreeva to face Svitolina in WTA Finals showpiece as Sabalenka apologises
articles.summary: Russian teen will face Ukraine star in the final. Sabalenka issues public apology after social media storm. The rise of Mirra Andreeva has seemed inevitable ever since she burst on to the tour as a precocious 15-year-old more than three years ago, but this week, six months after her maiden grand…
body: A year ago, Andreeva surprisingly failed to qualify for the WTA Finals, missing out by a paltry six points after bizarrely deciding not to compete in the final tournament week before the event. The world No 3 has been utterly supreme in her long-awaited debut appearance, bulldozing through elite opposition to reach the final without dropping a set. She has conceded just 18 games in four matches this week, including a 6-4, 6-0 demolition of the No 1 seed Aryna Sabalenka, winning 11 games in succession from 1-4 down.

Andreeva will rise to No 2 in the WTA rankings for the first time in her career on Monday regardless of the outcome here. The world No 1, Elena Rybakina, and No 3, Sabalenka, will both be defending a large number of points at the Australian Open after Rybakina defeated Sabalenka in this year’s final, which means the No 1 ranking will almost certainly be a realistic target for Andreeva at the start of the 2027 season, particularly if she closes out this imperious week with a title.

articles.title: Pulisic double leads US to 6-0 rout of Haiti in Pochettino’s farewell tour
articles.summary: US take 5-0 lead in Nations League quarter-final. Hall, 18, scores again as Pochettino prepares for exit. Pulisic goes into fourth on all-time US scoring list. When Mauricio Pochettino named his US roster for the November window, few could have expected that the games would double as his brief…
body: Saturday finally allowed Pochettino and his players to get on with the intended purpose of this window, and they took to the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals with aplomb. The US opened their two-leg series against Haiti with a dominant 6-0 victory in front of a considerably pro-Haitian crowd in Miami. Auston Trusty provided the first half’s only goal before Julian Hall, Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun contributed to the eventual rout.
Concacaf allowed Haiti to host the match in Miami under an “exceptional hosting arrangement” because of the ongoing political unrest and gang violence in Port-au-Prince.

Pochettino’s penultimate lineup as US manager built on the momentum fostered during the previous international window. Tyler Adams retained the captain’s armband after being named permanent skipper in September, a decision on which Pochettino’s successor would be foolish to renege.

articles.title: The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history
articles.summary: After scoring his first international goal in the 1-0 win over Ukraine, Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill says Terry Devlin is "a bit of a dream" to manage.
body: When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind.
And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far.

Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast.

They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner.

articles.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka apologises and denies claims she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian.
body: A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday.
Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general.
Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans.
"I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote.

articles.title: Ireland shake off sluggish start to brush aside Fiji
articles.summary: Ireland recover from a sluggish first-half performance to wear down spirited Fiji and keep alive their hopes of topping the Nations Championship northern hemisphere table.
body: After thumping Argentina last week, Ireland failed to click in an unconvincing opening, with Tommy O'Brien's early try and a Robert Baloucoune double enough for a 17-15 lead.
Fiji arrived in Dublin without a win in nine previous meetings against their hosts, and having been thrashed 54-17 by France last week.
But they dreamed of a historic win after tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, and a Ben Volavola penalty, kept them firmly in the contest at the break.
However, Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and O'Brien crossed as Andy Farrell's men scored 26 unanswered second-half points to deny the Pacific Islanders, who remain without a point in the competition.

articles.title: Littler opens bid for third Grand Slam crown with stunning Greaves win
articles.summary: Luke Littler started his pursuit of a Grand Slam of Darts hat-trick with a commanding 5-2 victory against Beau Greaves in Wolverhampton on Saturday night.
body: In a Group A blockbuster, 'The Nuke' struck seven maximums and a 109.97 average to defeat the Women's Matchplay champion.
Littler has yet to taste defeat in 15 Grand Slam matches, as he bids to join Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen by becoming the third player to win three successive titles in the West Midlands.
Greaves had memorably beaten Littler in the semi-finals of last year's World Youth Championship, but the back-to-back world champion had revenge on his mind.

After looking invincible in the first half of 2026 as he won the first five majors, Littler had come up short at the World Series of Darts Finals, then slipped to a first-round exit at the Grand Prix before another last-eight defeat in the European Championship.

articles.title: Devlin nets first international goal as Northern Ireland beat Ukraine
articles.summary: Terry Devlin's first international goal kept Northern Ireland top of their Nations League group as a 1-0 win over Ukraine set up a promotion decider away to Hungary on Tuesday.
body: The 23-year-old Devlin has been in the goals for Portsmouth this term with four, and opened his Northern Ireland account with a fine strike in the 68th minute as he left Ukraine goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin flat-footed with a shot from distance.

Pierce Charles then made a superb save to deny Danylo Sikan at the death and preserve Northern Ireland's fifth straight clean sheet - the first time they have achieved that since 2017 - and ensure they remain the only side in the competition yet to concede.

The three points put Northern Ireland back on top of Group B2 after Hungary's 2-0 win over Georgia earlier in the afternoon, and ruled Ukraine out of contention as they lost three straight matches for the first time in six years.

A draw in Budapest would be enough to elevate Michael O'Neill's young side to League A, while even in defeat they would face a play-off in March, and they have also earned a pot two place in next month's Euro 2028 draw.
